title: Ostrogoths
capsule: The Ostrogoths, an eastern Gothic confederation, emerged as a distinct political force after the collapse of Hunnic hegemony following Attila's death in 453, establishing themselves in Pannonia as foederati of the Eastern Roman Empire. Under Theoderic the Great, who assassinated the rival chieftain Odoacer at a banquet in Ravenna in 493, the Ostrogoths ruled Italy as a kingdom that maintained Roman administrative structures, law, and senatorial culture while the Gothic military elite held military command. The polity's collapse came through Justinian I's Gothic Wars (535–554), in which the generals Belisarius and Narses progressively destroyed Gothic resistance; the last king, Teia, fell at the Battle of Mons Lactarius in 553, and Italy reverted to nominal Byzantine control.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Ostrogothic control of Italy is well documented in late antique sources and archaeology; the attestation window in this dataset (455–500) covers the period before Theoderic's Italian conquest and reflects their Pannonian phase, which is somewhat less precisely bounded.
